newsitem.title: UK: NatWest falls after options loss revealed.
newsitem.headline: NatWest falls after options loss revealed.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc were lower on Thursday after the bank revealed it would take a higher than expected net charge of 77 million stg following losses in interest rate options.
The shares fell 5p to 739p by 0918 GMT.

The bank said the losses were confined to its interest rate options area and had started in late 1994. Four members of staff had been suspended and bonuses totalling 8 million stg will not now be paid out.
The losses were first revealed two weeks and estimates of the total cost were about 50 million stg.
"The number is substantially larger than people were expecting," said one equities salesman. "But the market had pretty much got on top of the situation already and had taken it out on the stock."
The shares have fallen 2.6 percent since news of the potential loss first broke.
"There will definitely be some questions asked," said a trader. "But possibly it will be one hell of an incentive to tighten up their management practices."
"But if they do that will they start limiting risk by limiting reward?...the two go hand in hand."
